item.title: Ye Loses Copyright Trial Over Uncleared ‘Donda’ Demo Sample
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our podcast, where we dive into the latest music news. Today, we're talking about Ye, formerly known as Kanye West, and a recent courtroom verdict that's making headlines.
[Short music transition]
Host: A jury has ruled that Ye must pay a significant amount in damages for failing to clear a sample in an early version of his Grammy-winning song "Hurricane" from his album Donda. The sample in question is from the instrumental track "MSD PT2", which was used in a demo of "Hurricane" that Ye played at a pre-release listening party in 2021.
[Short music transition]
Host: The verdict, which came after a week-long trial, holds Ye and his companies liable for infringing on the copyrighted track. The jury has ordered Ye to share a portion of his profits from the listening party, which was streamed live on Apple Music, with the owners of the sample. The total amount of damages is reportedly around $438,000, although Ye's team claims it will be limited to $176,000.
[Short music transition]
Host: Ye's team has responded to the verdict, calling it a "failed shakedown" and claiming that the plaintiffs had initially sought $30 million in damages. The Yeezy spokesperson also pointed out that the plaintiffs spent millions of dollars in legal fees for this outcome.
[Short music transition]
Host: The lawsuit was filed in 2024 by the producers of "MSD PT2", who alleged that Ye had used their track without permission in both "Hurricane" and another song, "Moon". Although the judge dismissed most of the lawsuit, the trial proceeded on the narrow issue of the early "Hurricane" demo, which included a direct sample of "MSD PT2".
[Outro music plays]
Host: That's all for today. Thanks for tuning in to our podcast. We'll be back with more music news and updates soon.
